Reference:
Oyler‐Yaniv, S., et al. (2017). "The Tunable Diffusion‐Consumption Mechanism of Cytokine Propagation Enables Plasticity in Cell‐to‐Cell Communication in the Immune System." Cell, 170(1), 21-32.


Claim: The cytokine communication mechanism is not influenced by the density of cytokine-consuming cells.

Abstract (A Tunable Diffusion‐Consumption Mechanism of Cytokine Propagation Enables Plasticity in Cell‐to‐Cell Communication in the Immune System):
&NA; Immune cells communicate by exchanging cytokines to achieve a context‐appropriate response, but the distances over which this communication happens is not known. Here, we used theoretical considerations and experimental models of immune responses in vitro and in vivo to quantify the spatial extent of cytokine communications in dense tissues. We established that competition between cytokine diffusion and consumption generated spatial niches of high cytokine concentrations with sharp boundaries. The size of these self‐assembled niches scaled with the density of cytokine consumers, a parameter that gets tuned during immune responses. In vivo, we measured interactions on length scales of 80–120 µm, which resulted in a high degree of cell‐to‐cell variance in cytokine exposure. Such heterogeneous distributions of cytokines were a source of non‐genetic cell‐to‐cell variability that is often overlooked in single‐cell studies. Oyler‐Yaniv et al. (2017) show that a simple diffusion‐consumption mechanism quantitatively describes the spatial spread of cytokines in vivo and results in localized niches of high cytokine concentrations that contribute to cell‐to‐cell variability.
